readme: Curated overlay applied to the reviewed integrations.sh snapshot during catalog import.
Keyed by exact canonical MCP URL. Every field is optional: a supplied value wins over the
snapshot, an omitted one falls through to the snapshot exactly as before.
Every entry must be backed by the provider's own current documentation, not inferred from an
aggregator. Use `notes` to record why a value was chosen so the reasoning survives review.
`featured` promotes an entry to the top of the connector catalog. `official` means the MCP
server is published by the provider on its own domain. Neither is a security review, and
neither may be presented as one.

entries.name: Gmail
entries.description: Search and read Gmail, create drafts, and organize messages through Google's official hosted MCP server.

presentation.introduction: Let agents work with the Gmail account you choose through Google's official hosted MCP server.

capabilities.title: Find and understand mail
capabilities.description: Search messages and threads, then use them as context for your work.

capabilities.title: Draft replies
capabilities.description: Prepare drafts for your review; sending stays in your hands.

capabilities.title: Organize the mailbox
capabilities.description: Work with labels, drafts, messages, and threads through the reviewed tools.

presentation.permissionSummary: Google asks for read, compose, and organize access to the mailbox you approve. OpenGeni exposes only the reviewed tools listed for this connector.

https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.re.label: Read your mail
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.re.description: Search and read messages and threads in the account you approve.

https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.co.label: Draft messages
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.co.description: Create and update drafts; nothing is sent without you.

https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.mo.label: Organize your mailbox
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.mo.description: Apply and remove labels on messages and threads.

notes: scopesHint keeps the consent surface to the union required by the reviewed tools instead of requesting every scope advertised by PRM.
allowedTools freezes the reviewed Developer Preview surface. Newly introduced remote tools stay unavailable until this contract is reviewed again.
connectionOwnership is personal_only: a consumer Gmail account is never a workspace credential. Each member authorizes their own mailbox.
logoSourceUrl is null because Google has not published a reusable Gmail MCP logo asset. Keep the self-hosted monogram rather than hotlinking a brand asset.

entries.name: Slack
notes: Slack's tools/list is grant-dependent. scopesHint is the complete set advertised by its official OAuth protected-resource metadata.
This is the personal hosted Slack MCP. The separate OpenGeni Slack bot is an Integration, not a catalog connector.
connectionOwnership is personal_only: the hosted Slack MCP is a human's grant. Shared workspace access is the OpenGeni bot, never a shared user token.

entries.name: Mobbin
entries.description: Search Mobbin’s library for real-world product screens, flows, and UI/UX references. Requires a paid Mobbin plan (Pro, Team, or Enterprise). Provider-managed usage credits apply.
notes: logoSourceUrl is null because Mobbin has not published a reusable logo license with its MCP listing. Keep the calm monogram rather than copying an unlicensed vendor asset.

entries.name: Linear
notes: Name only. Tier, provenance, auth kind, and scopes stay snapshot-derived.

Linear advertises CIMD but only issues MCP-accepted tokens to DCR clients; oauthProfile.clientSource expresses that compatibility override as data (the OAuth client also keeps the issuer on its prefer-DCR list for deployments with a stale catalog).

entries.name: HubSpot
entries.description: CRM contacts, companies, deals, and tickets from the HubSpot account you connect.
notes: Name only plus docs. Tier, provenance, auth kind, and scopes stay snapshot-derived: integrations.sh detected the server (mcp:initialize) and its OAuth metadata.

official is checkable: mcp.hubspot.com is under the snapshot domain hubspot.com. The /anthropic path is the endpoint integrations.sh detected; HubSpot's remote MCP server documentation is linked as documentationUrl.

Earlier snapshots skipped hubspot.com as auth_unknown because the aggregator had no credential entry for the surface. The refreshed upstream discovery document now carries hubspot_mcp_oauth_app (oauth2).

entries.name: Atlassian

notes: Snapshot name was the bare domain 'jira.com'. Upstream discovery for atlassian.com no longer lists an MCP surface, so the Rovo server row is keyed to jira.com; the earlier atlassian.net row for the same endpoint is superseded by this one.
Not marked official: the server is Atlassian's own but lives on mcp.atlassian.com, which is not mechanically checkable against the snapshot domain jira.com. official must stay a checkable claim.

entries.name: Intercom
entries.description: Conversations, contacts, and help center content from the Intercom workspace you connect.
notes: authKind is curated because the aggregator surface has no credential entry (auth status unknown), which would skip the row as auth_unknown. Intercom's own MCP guide documents the OAuth flow as the recommended authentication for mcp.intercom.com/mcp, and the server publishes RFC 8414 authorization-server metadata with dynamic client registration at https://mcp.intercom.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server. The row itself is upstream evidence with a real probe result; only the auth kind is overlaid.
Not marked official: the server is Intercom's own but the snapshot domain is intercom.io while the server lives on mcp.intercom.com. official must stay a checkable claim.
Not featured: Intercom was not on the reviewed featured list.
